title: Two Unchecked Boxes Made Citibank Wire $900 Million by Mistake
alt_title_1: Inside the Software Screen Behind Citibank's $900M Error
alt_title_2: How One Citibank Wire Typo Rewrote 88% of Loan Contracts
description_hook: On August 11, 2020, Citibank intended to wire $7.8 million in Revlon interest but accidentally wired nearly $900 million of its own funds after missing two Flexcube software checkboxes. By 2026, erroneous-payment clauses appear in 88% of corporate credit agreements.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 5-Hour Asset Builder OS + reading list
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Look at Figure 1 from the court opinion in Scene 2. Would you have caught that UI trap? Full court PDF is linked in the description.

scenes.headline: Meant $7.8M. Wired $900M.
scenes.narration: Citibank meant to wire 7.8 million dollars in interest for Revlon. Instead, it accidentally wired almost 900 million of its own money.
scenes.source: In re Citibank Aug. 11, 2020 Wire Transfers, Opinion p. 2 (S.D.N.Y. 2021)

scenes.headline: The Actual Flexcube Screen
scenes.narration: Here is Figure 1 from the court opinion. Staff ticked PRINCIPAL and three people approved it, but FRONT and FUND also needed ticks to stop the wire.
scenes.source: In re Citibank, No. 20-cv-6539, Opinion Figure 1, p. 13 (S.D.N.Y.)

scenes.headline: Lenders Kept $500 Million
scenes.narration: Ten firms refused to return over 500 million dollars. A trial judge let them keep it in 2021 before an appeals court reversed the ruling in 2022.

scenes.headline: Rewrote 88% of Loan Contracts
scenes.narration: Wall Street never forgot. By September 2026, erroneous payment clawback clauses sit inside 88 percent of corporate credit agreements.

scenes.headline: Fix Defaults, Not Just People
scenes.left_body: Three eyes missed a confusing screen
scenes.narration: Three human reviewers still missed a bad software default. High-stakes systems need clearer screens, not just extra signatures.
